title: Intersection numbers of pulled-back invertible sheaves scale by the degree of the morphism restricted to the subscheme
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter varieties.tex, section on numerical intersections
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file varieties.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves (f^*L_1 ... f^*L_d . Z) = deg(f|_Z : Z -> f(Z)) (L_1 ... L_d . f(Z)) for a morphism of proper schemes over k and an integral closed subscheme Z of dimension d. The proof computes the left side as the coefficient of n_1...n_d in an Euler characteristic, rewrites it as the alternating sum of the chi(X, R^i f_*O_Z tensor L^{n}) using a cited Euler-characteristic morphism lemma and the projection formula, and splits into two cases (proof lines 10492-10508). When dim f(Z) < d the total degree is < d and the claim is void; when dim f(Z) = d it uses dimension theory to see the generic point of Z is the unique point over the generic point of f(Z), deduces that f|_Z is generically finite with degree equal to the length of the stalk of f_*O_Z, and kills the higher direct images near that point (proof lines 10508-10536). H2: the generic-finiteness and length identification together with the higher-direct-image vanishing are the non-routine steps.
